architecture_decisions.justification: Lakehouse partitioned write and rename operations execute in O(1) constant time instead of O(N) copy-delete operations, preventing pipeline compute timeouts.

architecture_decisions.chosen_approach: System-Assigned Managed Identity (SMI) with Azure RBAC
architecture_decisions.alternative_considered: Storage Account Shared Keys & Connection Strings
architecture_decisions.justification: HIPAA compliance strictly forbids static unrotated keys in application configs. SMI eliminates credential theft risk and maintains full Entra ID audit trails.

architecture_decisions.chosen_approach: Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR) via Outbound HTTPS 443
architecture_decisions.alternative_considered: Opening Inbound Firewall Ports or Site-to-Site VPN
architecture_decisions.justification: Zero inbound firewall ports opened into private clinical LAN. Polling model over TLS 1.3 eliminates external attack vectors.

architecture_decisions.alternative_considered: Daily Full Table Reloads or Database Change Tracking
architecture_decisions.justification: Allows idempotent, light-touch incremental loads without altering vendor EMR database schema with triggers or expensive CDC transaction logs.

technical_questions.question: Why use System-Assigned Managed Identity over Storage Account Access Keys or SAS tokens in enterprise healthcare migrations?
technical_questions.core_rationale: Storage keys provide root-level administrative access to all data with no expiration or identity audit trail, violating HIPAA security guidelines. Managed Identity provides token-based, auditable, zero-secret access governed strictly by Entra ID RBAC.

technical_questions.question: Why is Hierarchical Namespace (HNS) mandatory for ADLS Gen2 in Medallion Lakehouse architectures instead of standard Blob Storage?
technical_questions.core_rationale: Without HNS, renaming or moving a directory requires copying every single blob individually (O(N) operations), which destroys pipeline performance at scale. HNS enables atomic metadata renames (O(1)) and granular POSIX directory ACLs.

technical_questions.question: How does a Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR) securely bridge on-premise databases without opening inbound firewall ports?
technical_questions.core_rationale: SHIR uses an outbound-only polling architecture over HTTPS port 443 with TLS 1.3. It never listens for inbound internet traffic, keeping the internal healthcare network completely secluded from external attacks.

technical_questions.question: How do you prevent data loss or duplicate ingestion if an incremental pipeline fails halfway through a run?
technical_questions.core_rationale: Through a two-phase watermark architecture where the watermark control table is only updated upon successful execution of the Copy Activity. If a failure occurs mid-batch, the old watermark remains, ensuring no records are skipped.

technical_questions.question: How does the upper watermark boundary enforce snapshot isolation if new rows arrive during an active Copy Activity?
technical_questions.core_rationale: The pipeline explicitly binds the extraction query to `updated_at <= new_watermark`. Any transaction occurring after the snapshot timestamp is excluded from the current batch and safely picked up in the next run when the old watermark advances to that exact snapshot boundary.

technical_questions.question: Where does compute and data serialization occur during on-premise to cloud data ingestion via SHIR?
technical_questions.core_rationale: The on-premise SHIR compute node queries the local SQL Server, serializes relational records into Parquet format in-memory, and pushes the payload over outbound port 443 to ADLS Gen2. Azure never initiates an inbound connection into the corporate hospital network.

technical_questions.question: Why did ADF throw 'property last_watermark_value doesn't exist' and how does output.firstRow vs output.value[0] work?
technical_questions.core_rationale: The PIVOT query generated 5 entity-specific columns (silver_patients, silver_providers, etc.), replacing the unpivoted last_watermark_value. When firstRowOnly is false, ADF outputs an array under value[], requiring array indexing output.value[0].<column>.

technical_questions.question: In a parallel DAG where SCR_Update_Silver_Watermark depends on all 5 Data Flows with 'Succeeded', what happens if one Data Flow fails?
technical_questions.core_rationale: Multiple incoming dependency arrows in ADF form an AND condition. If one Data Flow fails, the downstream script is skipped entirely. None of the watermarks advance, preserving transactional state consistency for automatic retry.

technical_questions.question: Why is salting mandatory when hashing SSNs under HIPAA Safe Harbor rather than raw SHA-256?
technical_questions.core_rationale: With a finite space of 1 billion 9-digit SSNs, raw SHA-256 hashes can be reversed instantly using precomputed rainbow tables. Salting introduces cryptographic entropy, making dictionary and rainbow table lookups impossible.

technical_questions.question: Why use an artificial surrogate key (patient_sk) in the Gold Star Schema instead of natural key patient_id?
technical_questions.core_rationale: Surrogate keys enable Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD Type 2) history tracking where multiple versions of a patient record share the same patient_id but have unique surrogate keys, preventing historical fact table joins from breaking. It also shields the lakehouse from upstream key reassignments or multi-system ID collisions.

technical_questions.question: Why compute age and cohort banding in the Lakehouse Spark pipeline rather than using DAX or Power Query in Power BI?
technical_questions.core_rationale: Centralizing feature engineering in the lakehouse ensures a single source of truth across all analytics consumers (Power BI, Synapse, Python/ML), eliminating conflicting departmental definitions. Furthermore, pre-computing on write preserves VertiPaq memory and avoids expensive runtime row-by-row compute during dashboard interactions.
